# Joint Rules

## Dovetails

- Pins and tails mate with no gaps wider than a pencil line.
- Tail angle sits between 1:6 for softwood and 1:8 for hardwood.
- Half-pins at the edges are at least half the width of a full pin, or they split under load.

## Mortise and Tenon

- Tenon thickness is about one third of the rail thickness.
- Tenon length reaches at least two thirds of the way through the leg for a blind joint.
- Haunch the tenon on a frame that takes a groove, so the groove does not leave a hole.
- Cheeks are parallel and the shoulders are square; a rocking tenon fails.

## Wood Movement

- Orient grain so wide panels float in grooves and never glue across the width.
- Cross-grain glue joints wider than about three inches fail with the seasons.

## Glue Surfaces

- Long grain to long grain is strong. End grain to anything is weak and needs a mechanical joint.
- Dry-fit every joint before glue and mark the parts.
